jamie: Anyone else seeing terraform plan for billing infra blow up after the module repo got a ref bump? CI plan shows a bunch of replaces. @sasha?
sasha: Which module / exact ref? paste the module block and a tiny plan snippet please.
jamie: Module block: `module \"billing\" { source = \"git::https://github.com/redwood/mod-billing.git?ref=v1.2.2\" }` — we were on v1.2.1. CI log shows:\n```\n# module.billing.google_service_account.sa will be replaced\n-/+ resource \"google_service_account\" \"sa\" { ... }\n```\nAlso, terraform refresh in CI kept hanging with `Another operation is in progress`.
olivia: :eyes: That looks like two issues: 1) state lock from CI causing refresh to hang, 2) module change causing a real or address drift. Check the backend lock first before forcing anything.
mike: If the module bumped but the resource addresses changed (or random IDs were introduced) plan will want replaces. Quick checks: `terraform init -upgrade` locally, `cat .terraform/modules/modules.json` to see module checksums, and `terraform state list | grep module.billing`.
sasha: Also compare before/after resource attributes: `terraform state show module.billing.google_service_account.sa` (in the current state) and the resource block in the new module code. Look for new `project`/`account_id` defaults etc.
jamie: CI actually failed with lock error: `Error: state lock in use: operation in progress (lock ID 4f2c1a...)` — looks like previous CI job crashed. Can someone confirm if it's safe to force-unlock?
olivia: If the lock holder is a dead CI run, force-unlock is fine. From a trusted machine: `terraform force-unlock 4f2c1a...` then re-run `terraform init -upgrade` and `terraform plan -target=module.billing` to isolate changes.
jamie: Doing the force-unlock now, will re-init and run a targeted plan. will update.
deploy-bot: CI #5421: terraform plan failed (exit code 2). Logs: https://ci.redwood.com/build/5421/logs
jamie: Unlock worked. Ran `terraform init -upgrade` and `terraform plan -target=module.billing`. Plan still wanted to replace the SA. Diff showed the module started setting `project = var.billing_project` on the SA resource (was implicit before) — so plan detects attribute change.
sasha: If the resource identity didn't change, you can import the new address to match existing resource instead of replacing. Example: `terraform import module.billing.google_service_account.sa projects/redwood-ops/serviceAccounts/billing-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
mike: If it's an address change (module ref relocated resource into a submodule), you may need `terraform state mv` or manual state edits, but only after careful review.
jamie: Import worked: `terraform import module.billing.google_service_account.sa projects/redwood-ops/serviceAccounts/billing-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` — reran plan, no changes. Thanks!
olivia: :thumbsup: Notes for future: 1) bump module refs in separate PRs so plan diffs are obvious 2) add a short changelog when module bump touches resource addresses 3) consider CI auto-unlock policy (ticket incoming).
mike: Filing ops ticket for CI auto-unlock timeout and better lock diagnostics, cc @olivia.
jamie: Closing this one — saved plan artifact to the build. Thanks everyone.
